appraisal_events.evidence: Françoise's words "Mademoiselle Albertine est partie" open "l'inimaginable enfer"; his strength fails, he sobs, must notify each of his selves in turn, and he concludes of the contest: "même l'emportant à la fin, tout de même dans le passé, c'est-à-dire irréparablement, je serais le vaincu."
appraisal_events.explanation: The passage narrates an unqualified collapse: he cannot rise, cannot renounce as he once did for Gilberte, admits he has grown "plus lâche", and names himself the loser of the contest whatever happens next.

appraisal_events.evidence: "Toute femme sent que, si son pouvoir sur un homme est grand, le seul moyen de s'en aller, c'est de fuir. Fugitive parce que reine, c'est ainsi"; her departure is likened to a state preparing its diplomacy by a demonstration of arms, and the woman who pleased him less than any passer-by becomes the one he would now prefer a thousand times.
appraisal_events.explanation: By leaving, Albertine converts her position entirely: the narration crowns her as sovereign precisely in flight and grants her the initiative he had spent a year denying her.

appraisal_events.evidence: "Pour Albertine elle-même, elle n'existait guère en moi que sous la forme de son nom"; "sa personne même y est pour peu de chose"; the beloved is "une figure que nous avions même peut-être oubliée, que nous pouvions connaître mal et croire médiocre" — "proportions minuscules de la figure de la femme".
appraisal_events.explanation: In a separate analytic movement the narration shrinks Albertine to a name written a thousand times on a wall, declaring that his anguish is about the ending of anxiety and not about her person at all.

status_effects.explanation: He is left without recourse by her flight, needing her return at any price and unable even to ask for it without losing more; the passage names him the vanquished.
Her departure seizes the whole leverage of the relation: she is the queen who flees, dictating terms while he calculates yachts, cars and marriage to get her back.
The same passage that crowns her as fugitive also declares her person nearly nothing in the drama, possibly mediocre and badly known, a mere name attached to a habit of anxiety.

ambiguities: The passage refuses to settle Albertine's motives — "Albertine avait-elle ainsi prémédité depuis longtemps sa fuite ?", "je ne vois rien sinon un petit fait" — so the reading of her flight as a calculated demonstration to extract better terms is the narrator's hypothesis, not established by the text.
